static_traits.name: Zhang Huilan
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to confide in, but has not yet shared troubles about reading pressure; recently reduced interaction with colleagues to read more, relationships growing tense, tending toward self-isolation
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior similar psychological problem history; have not yet received psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, can describe trigger situations and feelings concretely; coherent thinking; low self-evaluation, often using 'should'-style self-demands; reserved and skeptical about change, but can cooperate with role playing exercises

basic_info.main_problem: The main issue I want to discuss is the pressure I feel to read more books, which has led to stress and a sense of inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: I need to find a better way to manage these feelings.
growth_experiences: Long-term guilt and self-inadequacy since divorce; in social situations involving family or when meeting new friends, worrying others see her as selfish for having no children, producing a judged sense of insecurity and shame; tending to avoid such socializing to reduce discomfort, a pattern gradually affecting work and daily life.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough / not knowledgeable and passionate enough, unable to handle the librarian role
My value depends on comparison with others (especially reading volume and breadth of knowledge)

special_situations.event: Seeing colleagues read extensively, or others discussing new books/newly released works
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not read as much as they do, it means I am not competent, not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Makes a strict reading plan, joins a book club, sacrifices social time to work overtime reading
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should read more, otherwise I am incompetent.

special_situations.event: Compares herself with colleagues in reading volume and range of topics
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not reached or exceeded the level of same-age colleagues, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting higher, more unrealistic reading goals to catch up with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have fallen behind, I am not as good as they are.

special_situations.event: Not yet completing unrealistic reading goals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach the goal, it proves my ability is insufficient and I am not professional enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blames and is harsh on herself, reduces socializing and keeps forcing herself to read
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed, I cannot do it.

special_situations.event: At social situations with family gatherings or meeting new friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have no children, others will see me as selfish and not worthy of respect
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids such social settings, investing more in work or reading to escape judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am selfish.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted as a professional and valuable person, able to be treated as an equal in socializing
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being judged as incompetent or selfish, thus being rejected or belittled
defense_goal: Reducing the chance of being judged through distance and avoidance to maintain a sense of security
Undoing the sense of inadequacy through high standards and overexertion, seeking outside recognition

object_relations.self_representation: The inadequate / incompetent one under comparison and judgment
object_relations.object_representation: Critical reviewers with harsh standards (colleagues, audiences)

object_relations.self_representation: Out of place in social situations, possibly blamed as a selfish outsider
object_relations.object_representation: Groups/strangers who judge people by whether they have children

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes assertive (confident/assertive) communication role playing exercises
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing the exercise as a test that may expose one's inadequacy and incompetence, fearing failure and judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle and concrete tone, using small steps and positive reinforcement; demonstrate first then invite following along, emphasizing 'practice is not an exam', accepting the client's hesitation, giving actionable sentence patterns and immediate feedback.

manifestations: To increase reading, reduces interaction with colleagues and avoids social occasions with family participation
Although having friends, not yet sharing own stress, tending to bear it alone
outcomes: Negative emotions accumulating, further affecting work performance and sleep and diet

manifestations: Demanding of self with 'should' and rigid standards (as a librarian must read more)
Internalizes external professional norms as the sole measure of self-worth
outcomes: Increased guilt and self-criticism, decreased sense of freedom
Persistent stress and sense of inadequacy, difficulty with self-acceptance

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently uses the self-demand 'I should read more'
Directly takes industry / peer standards as the basis for self-worth evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Skeptical about change (like 'I am not sure whether I can do it' / 'not expecting miracles')
Worries excessively about failure before practice, expresses cautiously, and tends toward self-reproach

positive_force: Having a stable career and professional background (Master's degree in library science), with basic interest and ability in reading
Willing to try new methods (like role playing exercises), staying somewhat open to change
Can clearly identify trigger situations and automatic thoughts (like 'should' phrasing)
Having proactively sought strategies (making a reading plan, joining a book club)
Having a certain social support (a few friends I can confide in)
negative_force: Marked tendency toward social comparison, over-reliance on external evaluation
Avoids socializing to escape being judged, leading to isolation and worsening negative emotions
Self-criticism after setting unrealistic goals, prone to all-or-nothing thinking
Persistent stress affects sleep and eating, further weakening functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social situations (especially gatherings with family or where new people must be met)
antecedent: Being in social settings involving family
Needing to talk with newly met people
target_behavior.core_reason: Worried others see her as selfish for having no children, with judgment and belittlement (mind-reading inference and shame-based fear)
target_behavior.function: Escaping being judged and the resulting discomfort
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships growing distant and tense, increased sense of isolation spreading to work and daily functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Setting excessively high reading goals guided by 'should read more', with self-blame and guilt when not yet achieved
antecedent: Sees colleagues reading a lot or others discussing new books / new releases
Facing situations at work related to discussing the new book
target_behavior.core_reason: Forming the core belief of 'I am incompetent' through peer comparison, trying to compensate for inadequacy with overexertion and gaining recognition
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control and external recognition through overinvestment, briefly easing the sense of inadequacy
target_behavior.consequence: Rising stress, intensifying guilt and self-criticism, along with affected sleep and diet, decline in work performance
